Bound deployment and AI-provider identities to the exact accepted CMP offer and compute-provider identity through AIProviderRegistry.computeProviderRef.
Bound accepted CMP resource, payer, canonical provider-derived beneficiary and accepted price, rejecting broadened or contradictory terms.
Synchronized canonical CMP running/result/verified evidence into the constrained AIJobManager lifecycle without creating duplicate compute economics or result authority.
Observed canonical CMP settlement and refund references while intentionally deferring compatibility escrow/custody reconciliation to AI-AUDIT-5.

implementation_summary: Added a runnable dependency-light off-chain provider runtime under services/420ai-provider instead of reviving stale provider code.
Kept protocol authority in canonical RPC/Registry/ComputeMarket state through a narrow injected canonical client; local queues and health state are explicitly non-authoritative.

Added domain-separated provider-signed execution manifests and receipts binding chain, ComputeMarket graph, AI/CMP request and job identities, assignment, provider/resource, model/workload, privacy/verification references, input commitment, canonical manifest hash, runtime identity, result commitment and bounded timing.
Added AES-256-GCM private-payload storage with assignment-scoped authenticated data, maximum retention, expiry deletion and no plaintext persistence in runtime workflow state.
Added bounded retry and stable receipt-derived idempotency with canonical-state reconciliation after transient failures or lost RPC responses.

Added replay-safe restart recovery: durable nonsecret signed manifest/receipt state can resume pending submission without re-decrypting or re-executing; interrupted execution requires an explicit re-execution path after canonical revalidation.
Added redacted observability and non-authoritative health reporting.
requirements_satisfied: A runnable off-chain 420AI provider service now exists and is built against the current repository's injected RPC/Registry/CMP service boundary rather than stale provider implementation assumptions.
Execution is refused on wrong chain, wrong ComputeMarket graph, wrong provider, unapproved resource, expired deadline or mismatched private-input commitment.
Execution manifests and receipts are provider-signed, domain-separated and scope-bound.
Private payloads are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM, assignment-scoped authenticated data and bounded retention/expiry.
Receipt submission uses bounded retry, stable idempotency identity and canonical-state reconciliation before duplicate submission.
Non-transient submission failures are not blindly retried.

Restart recovery trusts canonical state, reconciles already-committed results, preserves pending receipt submission without rerunning inference and requires explicit re-execution for interrupted workloads.
Operational logs recursively redact private payload, prompt, token, secret, credential and raw byte fields.
Health reporting is operational only and never claims protocol authority.
The runtime does not create custody, settlement, verifier, governance, validator, identity or arbitrary lifecycle authority.
security_adversarial_invariant_results: Signed execution-object tampering fails verification.
Private payload ciphertext does not contain plaintext, wrong authenticated scope is rejected and expired payloads are deleted.
Local replay returns the same submitted receipt state without a second execution or second canonical submission.
Transient submission failures retry only within bounded attempts/deadline; non-transient failures do not retry.
A lost RPC response after canonical success reconciles from canonical state instead of submitting a duplicate receipt.
Pending signed receipt state survives restart and resumes without private-payload decryption or workload re-execution.
Interrupted execution cannot silently rerun; an explicit retryExecution path is required after canonical revalidation.
Wrong chain, ComputeMarket graph, provider, resource, deadline and input commitment fail before successful execution/submission.
Terminal canonical jobs remain terminal during restart recovery.
Observability redacts private payloads, prompts, tokens, secrets, credentials and raw buffers.
